claims.statement: Domain directories hold portable records and rules for hosts, credentials, connections, sessions, transfers, shell commands, sync and templates rather than live transports or concrete storage, and forbidden imports are checked by ArchitectureBoundaryTests.

Application owns portable use-case and feature state, including broad HostLibraryModel projections, connection journey/trust/retry coordination, and remote-filesystem and repository ports instead of concrete storage and transports.

Application Agent coordinates conversation execution through an injected registry and AgentKit services; Remote Infrastructure Agent registers host resolution, SSH/SFTP, metrics and scratch-transfer capabilities alongside runtime-owned tools.

Persistence owns the V52 schema and migrations: V47/V48 evolve Tailscale, V49 removes durable command/SFTP history, V50 adds cleanup, V51 adds Snippet colors with a frozen historical shape, and V52 removes retired terminal keyword-highlighting preferences. Snippet wire V1/V2 compatibility is independent of local schema versions.

Infrastructure's explicit CloudKit category coordinators use Persistence journals and scoped safety storage through CloudSyncLifecycleSafety and a shared lifecycle while retaining independent engines; incoming and conflict records go through the same receive validation path, and the SwiftData container disables automatic CloudKit storage.

General Infrastructure separates RevenueCat-backed Pro access and purchase-status services (not direct StoreKit transaction ownership), launch-file logging, attachment/skill imports, metrics parsers and Apple speech recognition; speech recognition receives injected audio input instead of owning native capture policy.

Remote Infrastructure SSH owns connection and channel protocol machinery while Transfers owns file-operation scheduling, transfer contexts and edit lifecycles; logical file admission, SSH session-channel admission and physical connection count are distinct controls.
Remote Infrastructure Security implements Keychain and key handling, SSHImport reads/stages concrete import sources, and Telnet is a separate transport rather than a path to SSH-only functionality.

Presentation contains shared forms, formatting, transcript state, SFTP and terminal presentation, and AppStrings semantic LocalizedStringResource definitions and shared formatting for both apps; architecture tests prohibit native UI, persistence and remote-infrastructure dependencies and app-local AppStrings owners.

Shared resources provide bundle localization, privacy/model metadata and distribution-icon catalogs/assets, while distribution-icon licensing is stored separately and platform-specific icons remain app-owned.

Device metadata remains reusable: Domain owns DeviceRecord, Application owns the directory model and port, and Persistence owns its repository and History journal adapter; clearing event history does not remove the device directory.

Xcode file-system-synchronized framework root groups are owned by their corresponding framework targets, while Frameworks/Resources is included by TFM, TFI, TermindWidgets and FrameworkTests rather than by the six shared framework targets; consumers of shared data must not assume it is in their framework bundle.

AssistantExecutionController freezes selected model/secret, permission mode, skills, tool registry and context at submission before optional asynchronous memory and compaction preparation, preventing later UI configuration changes from changing a captured turn.

Application tracks one cancellable agent preparation per conversation, prevents overlapping runs, persists missing-model or missing-credential failures before projecting them to conversation state, and can record interruptions on cancellation; injected AgentRunPersisting keeps SwiftData out of this coordination layer.

The controller composes AgentKit runtime with injected host-tool registry, eligible skill/memory tools, an ordered event channel, and weak conversation approval interaction that denies when closed; compaction is persisted before changing the observable transcript.

SwiftDataAgentRunRepository deduplicates history by message ID across successive run snapshots and stores frozen replay/context backing separately from ordinary messages; it restores transcripts in run order with compaction projection and recovers recorded tool results absent from a later transcript snapshot.

Agent persistence marks unfinished runs interrupted on repository initialization; editing truncates a conversation suffix and stages a replacement user run that a real run later adopts without duplicating the message, while conversation deletion removes its related tool and message backing and tombstones prevent late saves.

RemoteCharsetStreamConverter converts valid bytes while preserving malformed or unrepresentable bytes in both directions, buffering incomplete characters until more input or verbatim finish; unavailable iconv and UTF-8 bypass unchanged.

The remote charset adapter is applied at SSH exec, PTY and SFTP boundaries and also in Telnet; the SSH PTY OSC 7 filter rewrites charset-encoded working-directory paths into percent-encoded UTF-8 for Ghostty, buffering fragmented frames and bounding incomplete payloads.

LinuxDistributionIconCatalog loads the distribution JSON from the main bundle, matches exact detected distribution ID before like IDs, and returns no entry if catalog or distribution is unavailable; product resources include Pi model catalog and overrides, but the model capability resolver is owned by the separately pinned AgentKit package and its bundle-search behavior is not established by this repository.

Shared application strings and bundle metadata have separate string catalogs from AgentKit text, and the repository localization check requires completed zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ja translations; Linux distribution assets, catalog and licensing are regenerated together from a pinned Simple Icons version rather than fetched during app use.

TermindPresentation/Strings owns app-facing resource definitions while Frameworks/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings supplies their app-bundle translations; single-platform text still belongs with shared copy, and copy-boundary and CJK catalog checks are run together.

DeviceDirectoryModel registers the current device through an injected repository, caches name lookups and reports storage failures without committing a failed rename; the SwiftData adapter atomically journals device updates and refuses launch registration that would resurrect a deleted device.

The Cloud sync lifecycle persists its recovery fence before creating an automatically syncing engine and fetches before sending, using scoped safety and capability checkpoints to decide whether a fresh snapshot is required.

A scoped quarantined CloudKit record blocks upload until supported reconciliation clears it within the same save; the safety adapter archives the full native-field record on decode failure, preserving unknown fields for a future reader, and History/Device filters blocked records by kind within their shared zone.

History and Device synchronize native records through distinct kind-scoped journal states and engines in a shared zone; the Vault coordinator excludes their record identities from Vault receive and upload paths and does not treat their deletion events as Vault deletions.

Presentation's swiftUIKey bridge preserves resource interpolation metadata for SwiftUI key-only APIs, but confirmationDialog titles must use LocalizedStringResource directly where supported; architecture tests enforce this for app call sites.

Shared app string catalogs are manually managed rather than safely pruned by single-target extraction flags; edited catalogs must be normalized, CJK localization checks validate the normalized form and complete zh-Hans/zh-Hant translations, and generated string symbols remain disabled in favor of AppStrings.

Before submission capture, the optional AssistantModelSelectionController persists or repairs a valid per-conversation Chat model choice; a storage failure aborts the turn, and Persistence stores those device-local choices separately from run replay and deletes them with the conversation.

Remote Infrastructure registers host-tool definitions and historical-card presenters alongside AgentKit built-ins; acting-only remote writes and scratch push are restricted by phase, and scratch pull/push are available only when a shared scratch workspace is injected.

AgentKit's loop, providers and host-neutral tools belong to a remote Swift package whose project minimum is 0.19.1; Termind integrates it and registers host tools rather than implementing package internals.

GRDBMemoryStore opens its dedicated SQLite database lazily in an actor, so disabled memory can be constructed without creating files; its independent migrations support full-text message search, learning activity and memory reference dates outside the SwiftData model container.

Application owns the injectable collaboration coordinator and store contract for created chats and delivery receipts; Persistence deduplicates receipts by source run and tool call, and saves the delivered transition with the originated target message rather than on an earlier in-memory event.

Application's Assistant notification coordinator observes conversation completion and pending interaction events using injected preference, focus, visibility and sender capabilities; it consumes suppressed events without replay on a later focus change.

Remote Infrastructure's AssistantToolRegistry builds AgentKit built-ins, Termind host tools and MCP definitions for tool-capable models, sharing a conversation-scoped scratch workspace across runs and isolating it between chats.

Presentation maps Domain terminal palettes to Ghostty themes and configurations, applies custom settings before font overrides, and resets font family before setting a user-selected family so typography wins over theme settings.
Termind consumes remote AgentKit through upToNextMajorVersion from 0.19.1, pinned to 0.19.1 in Package.resolved; sibling working-tree edits do not enter Xcode builds until released and re-resolved.

Cross-repository AgentKit changes require package testing/release before advancing Xcode's minimum requirement and resolved revision together; resolved-only native builds avoid silently advancing the dependency and do not consume a sibling working-tree edit.

CloudSyncLifecycle confirms an enabled category and available account, binding sync to a scoped account/environment and stopping for explicit confirmation on an unexpected account change instead of automatically merging.

Recovery, capability mismatch or invalid serialized CKSyncEngine state trigger a fresh Cloud snapshot; on a successful fetch the lifecycle completes replica inventory and capability checkpoints before opening the send gate, while failed fetches leave uploads fenced.

The Cloud sync lifecycle reconciles engine pending changes with durable journal mutations, blocks unjournaled or quarantined changes during synchronous batch materialization, persists deletion handoff before batch delivery, and retires the engine on persistence or callback failure.

On macOS, the Persistence container factory acquires a nonblocking file-store lock before opening or migrating SwiftData; canonicalized same-process containers share the lease until their last owner closes, while another process fails with inUse, and the stable lock file is retained on release.
The container factory skips file locking for in-memory stores and rejects the combination of an in-memory store and explicit file URL; separate file stores can coexist.

Native macOS and iOS assistant owners inject Remote Infrastructure's registry factory into Application's execution controller, supplying the conversation, model, settings, event channel and host collaborators instead of placing concrete tool creation in Application.

The remote registry chooses native or local web search according to AI preference and provider capability, resolves usable MCP server credentials, and builds the catalog with AgentKit built-ins before Termind host tools and discovered MCP tools so they cannot shadow built-in names.

Infrastructure's live Pro controller requires a valid RevenueCat configuration from the app bundle; without it, refresh fails closed as verificationFailed rather than running a fallback StoreKit purchase observer, while app entrypoints choose live versus test access.

RevenueCat purchase service uses anonymous SDK users and StoreKit 2 within the SDK; it fetches current customer info, streams customer-info changes, attempts one non-test migration sync for a previously unentitled user, and uses SDK-cached information if fetching fails.

The RevenueCat resolver grants Pro only for a verified configured entitlement in an eligible active phase and rejects refunds, billing retry, expiration and failed verification; ProAccessController coalesces refreshes and prioritizes newer stream updates over older fetches, scheduling refresh at the active subscription deadline.

The shared privacy manifest declares no tracking and unlinked crash, diagnostic and device-ID collection for app functionality, with UserDefaults, system boot time and file timestamp accessed-API reasons; its bundle placement is a product-resource boundary rather than a framework-bundle guarantee.

Pro access values are Domain-owned, RevenueCat status and gating are Infrastructure-owned, and apps own their paywall presentation; requiring an unavailable feature opens paywall, while paywall completion refreshes status without automatically dismissing it.

TerminalFindController owns query/presentation through injected actions and focus. Changed queries and navigation are fenced during resize suspension; dismissal retains query, and resume/reopening only restarts a presented nonempty query when not suspended.

Terminal Find state is owned by native session/workspace models rather than a transient mounted search field; macOS SSH sessions and mobile workspaces inject terminal binding execution and focus requests into the shared controller.

TerminalFindController.dismiss(restoringFocus:) defaults to invoking the injected focus callback but can end search without requesting terminal focus; the mobile workspace search binding selects restoringFocus: false so UIKit responder transitions and dismissal guarding remain in the app-owned toolbar search controller, not shared Application or Presentation.

TerminalFindControllerTests verify default focus restoration, retained-query restart, empty-query navigation suppression, and repeated native dismissal emitting only one end action without requesting terminal focus.
